title: Inference Fabric
subtitle: A throughput-first GPU inference pipeline on consumer NVIDIA hardware: broker, saturated runtime, completion, vector store

stats.label: hand-written CUDA kernel families, native Blackwell binaries, no JIT
allocations after the first second of a profile, down from 4,236
tasks on one GPU over ten hours, zero retries
lines of first-party Rust, C++ and CUDA across six trees

lede: Large offline model workloads are throughput problems. Synthetic data, probe generation, hidden-state extraction and bulk embedding analytics do not care about response time; they care whether the GPU is busy. A request-and-response serving stack wastes GPU time on padding and idle gaps and ties producers to GPUs for hours. I built the Inference Fabric for throughput. Producers drop millions of tokenised tasks and walk away. A broker that understands tokens organises the work so GPUs barely pad. Pull-based GPU workers stay saturated on mixed hardware. Results land in the database when they finish. Vector outputs flow into a GPU-native store that searches and scores cluster quality.
quote: I did not replace NVIDIA's inference; I fed it.
evidence: High-throughput batch inference: a 7-billion-parameter dense model in FP8 at 163,000 tokens per second on two NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, and 4.95 M tasks on one GPU over ten hours with zero retries.

Token-aware scheduling: a durable broker on memory-mapped append-only logs that groups work by token shape and packs to each GPU's declared limits, with 0.42% padding waste and 99.9% prefix cache hits across two cards.

TensorRT and TensorRT-LLM engineering: a pull-based saturation runtime around stock TensorRT-LLM kernels with a zero-allocation hot path, 4,236 allocations in the first second of an Nsight profile and none after.

CUDA kernel development: fifteen hand-written kernel families compiled to native Blackwell binaries with no JIT, computing 38 per-cluster health metrics and exact, inverted-file and lattice vector search, each with a CPU reference.

Distributed systems correctness: work retired only when its completion is acknowledged, so a restart never re-runs work the GPUs already hold, with 12.3 B tokens received and 12.3 B routed, a difference of zero.
Cloud GPU provisioning with cost controls: one call stands up a consumer node locally, on a LAN host over mutual TLS or on rented cloud spot capacity, behind a fail-closed daily dollar budget.
author: Corey James
